fd543cb36d7ed24db4e6054a23fe4d0004359f4a.summary: An overview article, part 1 of 2, on user-mode dynamic hooking: placing hooks at runtime to intercept and redirect program execution. It covers IAT hooking, LD_PRELOAD library hooking, inline hooking and the Microsoft Detours framework, and notes uses in tracing, HIDS/HIPS, reverse engineering and rootkits.

tools.q: Microsoft released a framework to help in placing inline hooks on Win32 API functions called Detours.

techniques.q: focuses on dynamic hooking, where hooks are placed at runtime in memory.
IAT hooking happens in user mode and is a relatively easy way to hook every call to a specific API
Inline hooking can be used in user mode, although similar techniques can also work in kernel mode.
The LD_PRELOAD environment variable specifies a list of libraries to load first when a program is executed,

hedges: The article assumes the reader already has sufficient access to modify a program's memory to place a hook.
IAT hooking is a user mode technique, which makes it easier to implement but also easier to detect, so it has limitations.
Address randomisation such as ASLR may make the simple return-address lookup approach impossible.

fdf53fac0af9cced76179fb1b9df0ce009952e36.summary: ESRC malware analysis (February 2022) of a malicious Word document disguised as a customer-center guide from Klip, a digital asset wallet service. When users enable content, macros run, drop an XML file that executes, and attempt to contact a command server. The server could not be reached, so analysis stopped there. The report links the threat to the Smoke Screen campaign and to Thallium (also known as Kimsuky), and describes the actor as North Korea-linked. It is currently detected as Trojan.Downloader.DOC.Gen.

fd01a4f0faec85d7c66faedba9e9dc8ab82fd6cb.summary: Sygnia, a vendor blog from 2024, describes how ransomware attacks against VMware ESXi and vCenter virtualisation environments typically unfold: initial access, privilege escalation, access validation, deployment on hosts, backup compromise, data theft for double extortion, and encryption. It names ransomware groups and tools, including LockBit, BlackCat and Akira, that it says often use this attack vector. It then gives defender guidance on monitoring, backups, authentication, hardening and network restrictions.
